references.text: Moses wrote down all the Lord's words, just as Joshua wrote down the words in God's book of the law.
Moses wrote the words of the law in a book, and Joshua continued this tradition by writing in God's book of the law.
Jacob set up a stone as a memorial, just as Joshua set up a large stone as a witness to the covenant.
Jacob buried the idols under the oak at Shechem, the same place where Joshua later set up the memorial stone under the oak in the sanctuary.
The story of Abimelech takes place at the oak in Shechem, the same holy place mentioned here.
Joshua set up twelve stones at Gilgal as a memorial, in a similar way to how he here sets up a large stone as a witness.
Joshua built an altar and wrote a copy of the Law of Moses on stones, showing his practice of writing and setting up memorials.
Samuel wrote down the rights of the kingdom in a book and placed it before the Lord, an action similar to Joshua's writing in God's book of the law.
Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer as a memorial, just as Joshua set up a large stone as a witness.
